clue.text: Den of Scottish landlord unfinished

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its end, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a laird is the owner of a landed estate in Scotland

explanation.surface: A Highland estate owner's hideaway, oddly left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: LAIRD loses its last letter to give LAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is the den or resting place of a wild animal, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Editor with superior purpose expressed disapproval

indicators.note: in a down clue superior means placed above, so the purpose word sits on top of the editor

parts.note: an object is an aim or purpose
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor whose boss has a different aim voices an objection.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the piece 'superior' to the editor is written above it, so OBJECT comes first, then ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To object is to protest or state opposition, so the past tense means voiced one's dislike.

clue.text: Endeavoured to change voters

indicators.note: to change the voters is to rearrange them, so its letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A campaigner tried hard to win the electorate round.
explanation.definitionFit: Strove is the past tense of strive, meaning tried hard or made an effort.

clue.text: Powerful people in business given special name tags

indicators.note: special suggests the letters are made into something out of the ordinary, a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: At a conference the big shots wear personalised badges.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnates are wealthy, influential tycoons who dominate an industry or trade.

clue.text: Madness with Left invading capital city

indicators.note: an invader gets inside territory, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: mania is wild madness
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Political chaos as the Left storms a nation's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside MANIA, between the N and the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Manila is the capital of the Philippines, so it is an example of a seat of government.

clue.text: Sad member of Boat Race crew?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: feeling low or down
second meaning: someone who has represented Oxford or Cambridge against the other at a sport

explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing contest on the Thames; its rowers win a university award named after a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means melancholy, and also names an Oxbridge athlete awarded colours for competing against the rival university.

clue.text: Bash attended by little woman somewhere south of the Thames

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or hit hard
Beth March is one of the sisters in the novel Little Women

explanation.surface: A rowdy party with a young woman as guest, held in south London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bash' looks like a party, but it is a verb meaning strike. Lambeth is a London borough on the south bank of the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambeth is a London district lying on the south bank, so it is one place across the river from Westminster.

clue.text: Competent father entertained by 14

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is inside the host's house, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the answer to 14 down, an urgent message
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A dad hosted by a politician proves himself a competent fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: A number in a clue points to another answer in the grid, here the one at 14 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable means having the ability or skill needed, a straightforward synonym of being up to the job.

clue.text: Something growing in street

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the word that follows, wrapped in it

parts.note: the middle four letters of the word

explanation.surface: A plant springing up in a city road.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree is a plant, and plants grow, so this vague description fits as a cryptic pointer.

clue.text: Move against enemy is causing resentment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a military attack, as a noun
second meaning: rude or insulting, as an adjective

explanation.surface: An attack on the foe is stirring up bitterness.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for an attacking campaign in war and an adjective for remarks that give insult.

clue.text: Engineers aboard aircraft or ship

indicators.note: people aboard a craft are inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a fighter is a combat aircraft
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: Military engineers boarding a plane or a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are a corps of the British Army, a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a vessel built to carry cargo, so it is a kind of ship.

clue.text: Coffee provided by hotel at ten

indicators.note: the words that follow provide the letters directly, spanning across them

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A hotel serves morning coffee at ten o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is an espresso drink made with lots of steamed milk, a type of coffee.

clue.text: Like an Oxford boy seen outside church

indicators.note: one piece seen outside another wraps around it

parts.note: a lad is a boy
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Oxford University student waiting outside a chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' suggests the university, but here it is a style of shoe fastened by laces.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford is a formal shoe tied with laces, so it is fastened that way.

clue.text: Charm of performer's first appearance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to enchant or delight, as a verb, stressed on the second syllable
second meaning: the moment an actor comes on stage

explanation.surface: An actor's charisma shows the moment they step onstage.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to hold spellbound; as a noun it means a coming on stage.

clue.text: Urgent message for prominent LibDem

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a telegram sent by wire
second meaning: Sir Vince, former leader of the Liberal Democrats

explanation.surface: An urgent note arrives for a leading Liberal Democrat politician.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Democrats are a British political party; Vince Cable led them from 2017 to 2019.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old term for a telegram and the surname of a well-known party leader.

clue.text: Chemical help to limit cold

indicators.note: to limit something is to hem it in, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: aid is help
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A remedy meant to keep a common cold in check.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside AID after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid is a kind of chemical compound, a substance that donates protons in a reaction.

clue.text: Artist died, wise person falling over

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees

indicators.note: something falling over is upended, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a sage is a wise person

explanation.surface: An artist's death, with an elderly wise man toppling over.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Degas was a French Impressionist painter famous for his ballet dancers.

clue.text: Wild Reds celebrate, putting on special attire?

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
to sing is to celebrate in song

explanation.surface: Delirious Liverpool fans celebrate by dressing up in team kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reds' is the nickname of Liverpool and Manchester United football fans.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing means putting clothes on, and the question mark admits that special attire narrows it a little.

clue.text: Model hugging British mug

indicators.note: one thing hugging another wraps its arms around it, enclosing it

parts.note: a toy can be a model, such as a toy car
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A fashion model embracing a British fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' is British slang for a fool, but here it is the drinking vessel. B goes inside TOY.
explanation.definitionFit: A Toby jug is a beer mug shaped as a seated man in a tricorn hat.

clue.text: Yon Conservative, the female PM once

parts.note: yon is an old word for that, over there
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
her is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: Pointing to a Tory woman who used to run the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher was the Conservative Prime Minister of the UK from 1979 to 1990.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatcher was Britain's first woman Prime Minister, so she is a former holder of that office.

clue.text: Notice in this location holy books for disciple

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a notice
here means in this place
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A sign here points the faithful follower towards the scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a supporter or follower of a cause or leader, as a disciple is.

clue.text: See pal, after an upset, go by

indicators.note: an upset knocks things over and out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Visit your friend after a quarrel and let things pass.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to elapse when it passes, so the verb means to slip by.

clue.text: Visionary born by stretch of water

parts.note: b is the abbreviation for born
a lake is a body of water

explanation.surface: A dreamer who began life beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: William Blake was an English poet and painter famous for his mystical visions and prophetic books.

clue.text: Animal noises that could come from stable

indicators.note: letters that could come from a word are reworked out of it into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sounds of livestock drifting out of a farm building.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleats are the cries made by sheep and goats, so they are calls of farm animals.

clue.text: Eatery that could provide a sir with beers

indicators.note: the letters could be worked up into something else, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the link word with dropped

explanation.surface: A restaurant able to serve a gentleman some ales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the two parts of the fodder and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal French-style restaurant, so it is a place to eat.

clue.text: Black liquid to turn into vapour

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
oil is a liquid

explanation.surface: Dark crude heated until it turns to gas.
explanation.definitionFit: To boil is to heat a liquid to the point where it changes into steam or gas.

clue.text: Small room's source of electric power

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a little room, as in a prison or monastery
second meaning: a battery unit producing current

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is', joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a tiny chamber for a prisoner or monk, and also a single unit of a battery.

clue.text: Final thing for a cobbler to work on

definitions.meaning: first meaning: coming at the end

definitions.text: thing for a cobbler to work on
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a foot-shaped block used by a shoemaker

explanation.surface: The final job left on a shoe repairer's bench.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means ultimate, and also names the wooden foot model a shoemaker shapes footwear around.

clue.text: Young lady, one no good, unable to be found

parts.note: miss is a title for a young unmarried woman
I is the Roman numeral for one
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A young woman, a bad lot, has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Missing describes something lost whose whereabouts nobody knows, so it cannot be located.

clue.text: His team may be troubled by such lack of belief

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed and stirred up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A manager frets that his side may be undone by unbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheism is disbelief in the existence of any god, so it is a lack of religious faith.
